target.title: fix(agents): skip sender-scoped tool policy when sender identity is absent
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A spawned subagent loses tools granted by an exact `toolsBySender` sender override because its internal session has no sender identity and falls through to the wildcard `"*"` policy, silently stripping filesystem and runtime tools.
- Problem: `resolveSenderToolPolicy` resolves sender-scoped tool policy in subagent sessions that have no sender identity, matching the wildcard `"*"` entry and stripping tools
- Solution: Detect subagent sessions via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` and skip sender-scoped policy resolution — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy
- What changed: `src/agents/conversation-capability-profile.ts` (skip sender policy for subagent sessions, same pattern as owner WebChat skip)
- What did NOT change: `sender-tool-policy.ts`, spawn/session lifecycle, config schema, tool policy for sessions with sender identity

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #109025
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

When a WhatsApp sender configured with an E164 `toolsBySender` override spawns a subagent via `sessions_spawn`, the subagent resolves its own tool policy. Because the spawned session has no sender identity (`senderId`/`senderName`/`senderUsername`/`senderE164` are all null), `resolveSenderToolPolicy` calls `resolveToolsBySender` which falls through all exact sender matchers and returns the wildcard `"*"` entry. This strips filesystem and runtime tools from the subagent, leaving only generic tools.

The parent already resolved the correct sender-scoped policy — the subagent inherits the parent's already-resolved tool policy and should not re-resolve sender-scoped restrictions without a sender identity.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: spawned subagent re-resolves `toolsBySender` without sender identity, matching wildcard `"*"` and losing filesystem/runtime tools
- Real environment tested: Linux, Node 22.22.3, `fix/subagent-sender-tool-policy-109025`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Resolver-level proof: three scenarios
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose

# Full-pipeline integration proof: parent + anonymous + subagent + subagent restrictions
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
```

- Resolver-level test output:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ whatsapp parent with E164 identity gets exact allow override 10ms
 ✓ anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 1ms
 ✓ spawned subagent skips sender policy (isSubagentEnvelopeSession detected) 149ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

- Full-pipeline integration test output (applyFinalPolicy through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy`):

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/effective-tool-policy.test.ts --run --reporter=verbose
 ✓ fix #109025: parent with E164 gets exact toolsBySender allow (no denies) 166ms
 ✓ fix #109025: anonymous user without sender identity gets wildcard deny 164ms
 ✓ fix #109025: spawned subagent skips sender policy, retains parent tools 207ms
 ✓ fix #109025: subagent restrictions still narrow tools after sender-policy skip 167ms

 Tests  16 passed (16)  (12 existing + 4 new)
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. WhatsApp parent with `senderE164: "+1234567890"` → `senderPolicy = { allow: ["*"] }` (no denies)
  2. Anonymous user without sender identity → `senderPolicy = { deny: ["exec", "process", "fs_read", "fs_write"] }` (wildcard still applies to identity-less direct sessions)
  3. Spawned subagent (session key `subagent:child::main`, detected via `isSubagentEnvelopeSession`) → `senderPolicy = undefined` (skipped)
  4. Spawned subagent with configured `subagents.tools.deny` → subagent restriction layer still removes intended tools after sender-policy inheritance
- What was not tested: WhatsApp/Telegram E2E with real `toolsBySender` config (requires real channel credentials)
- **Fix completeness pre-check (4 questions)**:
  - ✅ Auth guard: the bypass is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` — only positively recognized subagent sessions skip sender policy
  - ✅ Enum completeness: subagent detection uses the existing session-key and envelope-based recognition — all subagent session shapes are covered
  - ✅ Path coverage: the guard sits in `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` before `resolveSenderToolPolicy`, covering all capability resolution callers
  - ✅ Cleanup symmetry: no state to clean up — `senderPolicy` is `undefined` for subagents, same as for owner WebChat sessions

## Root Cause

`resolveSenderToolPolicy` → `resolveToolsBySender` → `matchToolsBySenderPolicy` falls through all exact sender matchers and returns `compiled.wildcard` when no sender field matches. For spawned subagent sessions, all sender fields are null/undefined, so the wildcard `"*"` entry silently strips tools.

- **Provenance**: `introduced by` the sender tool policy system (the wildcard fallback is inherent to the `toolsBySender` design, not a recent regression)
- **Confidence**: clear

## Regression Test Plan

The fix is validated by two test files:
- `proof-109025-sender-tool-policy.test.ts` — 3 resolver-level scenarios (parent, anonymous, subagent)
- `effective-tool-policy.test.ts` — 4 integration scenarios through the full `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy` pipeline (parent, anonymous, subagent, subagent + restrictions)

Existing tests (13 capability-profile tests, 16 effective-tool-policy tests, 20+ group-policy tests) continue to pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Subagent sessions spawned with `sessions_spawn` from a sender-trusted conversation will now retain filesystem and runtime tools instead of having them stripped by the wildcard sender policy.

## Security Impact

**All checkboxes must be checked or explained**

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No — subagent-only exemption; identity-less direct sessions still get the wildcard
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: WhatsApp E164 parent → exact allow; anonymous user → wildcard deny; subagent → senderPolicy skipped; subagent + restrictions → subagent deny still applies
- Full-pipeline proof: integration tests run through `resolveConversationCapabilityProfile` → `applyFinalEffectiveToolPolicy` — the same path used in production for effective tool inventory resolution
- Edge cases checked: session detected by `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` vs anonymous session; subagent with `spawnedBy` set; subagent restrictions applied on top of inherited sender policy
- What you did NOT verify: real WhatsApp E2E with `toolsBySender` config (requires channel credentials)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — sessions with sender identity are unaffected; only subagent resolution changes
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Gating on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` in `conversation-capability-profile.ts` is the correct boundary — it follows the same pattern as the existing `isOwnerInternalSession` skip, and only positively identified subagent sessions are affected.
- **Refactor needed**: No
- **Alternative considered**: Passing sender fields through subagent spawn metadata was rejected (4+ files, ~30 lines). Adding `hasAnySenderIdentity` to `sender-tool-policy.ts` was tried and reverted because it incorrectly exempted anonymous direct sessions.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Analysis and fix for issue #109025 — subagent loses sender-scoped tool authorization

## Risks and Mitigations

**Low risk**: The exemption is gated on `isSubagentEnvelopeSession` which only matches sessions with known subagent session keys or stored ACP envelopes with subagent metadata. Anonymous direct sessions and WebChat users without sender identity still get the wildcard deny policy as expected.

---

Fixes #109025
